Let
\[
e_n(u)=\exp(2\pi i u/2^n),\qquad m=2M+1.
\]
The sum separates as
\[
A_{M,K}(r,s,t)=G(r,s)\,H(t),
\]
where
\[
G(r,s)=\sum_{x,y\bmod 2^m} e_m(x^2-xy+y^2-rx-sy)
\]
and
\[
H(t)=\sum_{z\bmod 2^m} e_m(3\cdot 2^{2K}z^2-tz).
\]

For the binary part, the matrix of the derivative of \(x^2-xy+y^2\) is
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det B=3,
\]
so \(B\) is invertible modulo \(2^m\). Completing the square gives
\[
G(r,s)=S_m\,
e_m\!\left(-3^{-1}(r^2+rs+s^2)\right),
\]
where
\[
S_m=\sum_{x,y\bmod 2^m} e_m(x^2-xy+y^2).
\]
A parity recursion gives \(S_n=4S_{n-2}\), and \(S_1=-2\). Since \(m=2M+1\),
\[
S_m=-2^m.
\]
Thus
\[
G(r,s)=-2^m e_m\!\left(-3^{-1}(r^2+rs+s^2)\right).
\]

For the \(z\)-part, write \(d=2K\) and \(n=m-d=2(M-K)+1\). Splitting \(z\) modulo \(2^n\) shows
\[
H(t)=0
\]
unless \(2^{2K}\mid t\). Writing \(t=2^{2K}\tau\), the remaining one-dimensional Gauss sum is zero unless \(\tau\) is even. Hence \(A_{M,K}(r,s,t)\neq0\) only when
\[
t=2^{2K+1}\beta,\qquad \beta\bmod 2^{2(M-K)}.
\]
For such \(t\),
\[
H(t)=2^{2K}2^{M-K+1}
\exp\!\left(2\pi i\left(\frac38-\frac{3^{-1}\beta^2}{2^{2(M-K)+1}}\right)\right).
\]

Therefore \(A_{M,K}(r,s,t)\) is real precisely when
\[
3^{-1}\left(r^2+rs+s^2+2^{2K}\beta^2\right)
\equiv 7\cdot 2^{m-3}\quad\text{or}\quad 3\cdot 2^{m-3}
\pmod{2^m}.
\]
The first case gives positive values and the second gives negative values. Multiplying by \(3\), this becomes
\[
r^2+rs+s^2+2^{2K}\beta^2
\equiv 5\cdot 2^{m-3}
\]
for positive values, and
\[
r^2+rs+s^2+2^{2K}\beta^2
\equiv 2^{m-3}
\]
for negative values.

Put \(h=M-K\). Then \(\beta\bmod 2^{2h}\). The binary form
\[
U(r,s)=r^2+rs+s^2
\]
is anisotropic modulo \(2\): if \((r,s)\not\equiv(0,0)\pmod2\), then \(U(r,s)\) is odd. Hence the number of solutions to
\[
U(r,s)\equiv a\pmod{2^m}
\]
is
\[
3\cdot 2^{m-1}
\]
whenever \(a\) has even valuation \(<m\), and is
\[
2^{m-1}
\]
when \(a\equiv0\pmod{2^m}\).

For the positive congruence, every \(\beta\) gives a nonzero right-hand side of even valuation, so
\[
P_{M,K}=2^{2h}\cdot 3\cdot 2^{m-1}
=3\cdot 2^{4M-2K}.
\]

For the negative congruence, the exceptional case occurs when
\[
v_2(\beta)=h-1,
\]
which happens for \(2^h\) values of \(\beta\bmod 2^{2h}\). Those give right-hand side \(0\), contributing \(2^{m-1}\) each; all other \(\beta\) contribute \(3\cdot 2^{m-1}\). Therefore
\[
N_{M,K}
=2^h\cdot 2^{m-1}+(2^{2h}-2^h)\cdot 3\cdot 2^{m-1}
=2^{2M}\left(3\cdot 2^{2M-2K}-2^{M-K+1}\right).
\]

\[
\boxed{(P_{M,K},N_{M,K})=
\left(3\cdot 2^{4M-2K},\;2^{2M}\left(3\cdot 2^{2M-2K}-2^{M-K+1}\right)\right)}
\]
